title: Opsight: usage/cost/latency watchtower for composite degradation detection
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: We are seeing subtle multi-signal degradations that individually are below per-metric thresholds but together indicate customer-visible regressions (e.g., small steady latency increase paired with slight per-token cost rise across a cohort). Opsight (watchtower) is a new backend pipeline + alerting layer that fuses per-tenant usage, cost, and latency telemetry to surface composite degradations early and route them appropriately.

Scope: implement a lightweight streaming enrichment + scoring pipeline in the console backend that: 1) materializes tenant-level baseline features (model mix, median seq len, plan tier), 2) computes composite signal scores using percentile baselining + Bayesian change-point detection, 3) exposes grouped alerts to the Console Alerting service with enriched context (top contributing routes, model family, token buckets affected), and 4) supports rate-limited automated runbook actions (mute, throttle sampling, create incident ticket).

Design notes / trade-offs:
- Data path: we will consume normalized usage telemetry from the existing Kafka topic (usage.events.v2), enrich with tenant profile from the materialized store (Cassandra), compute aggregations in a streaming job (Flink). Chosen for low-latency enrichment and stateful windows.
- Scoring: use a hybrid approach: percentile-based short-window scoring for spikes + Bayesian Online Change Point Detection (BOCPD) for gradual drifts. This balances sensitivity and false positive control.
- Storage vs resolution: full-minute resolution for top-10% tenants (by spend) and adaptive downsampling (5/15-min) for long-tail tenants to cap cost. This reduces storage by ~70% vs uniform minute-level retention with acceptable detection latency for tail tenants.
- Routing policy: alerts carry a probabilistic severity (0-1) and metadata tags (tenant_tier, estimated_cost_impact, affected_models). Severity -> routing mapping configured in Console (enterprise alerts -> on-call, free-tier -> email digest).
- Explainability: alert payload includes tokenized contributing factors and a 3-step local explanation (change magnitude, model family shift, recent rollout). This supports on-call triage and PM feedback loops.

Non-goals: not implementing automated rollback or model-level intervention in this ticket. Not replacing metric-level SLO alerts; the watchtower complements them with composite scoring.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Streaming job processes usage.events.v2, enriches with tenant profile, and emits composite_score events for >=95% of top-100 tenants with end-to-end latency < 30s.
2) Score computes both spike and drift components and exposes contributing factor fields (cost_delta_pct, latency_delta_ms, model_family_shift).
3) Console Alerting accepts watchtower alerts and routes them according to tenant_tier. Demo: a seeded scenario for a mid-tier tenant shows an alert in Console with explanation and linked runbook.
4) Storage budget respected: tail-tenant retention meets the adaptive downsampling spec and overall storage increase <= 15% for the rollout.
5) Unit + integration tests for scoring, enrichment joins, and routing mappings.
6) Observability: dashboards (Grafana) with heatmaps for composite scores and an SLI for false-positive rate under labeled test corpus < 7%.
tasks: Design streaming Flink job and state schema
Implement enrichment consumer for usage.events.v2 and join to tenant_profile view
Implement composite scoring library (percentile baselining + BOCPD) with unit tests
Add adaptive downsampling logic and storage budget guardrails
Wire alert output to Console Alerting API with routing metadata
Create Grafana dashboards and alerting runbook entries
Performance test on staging with synthetic load representing 10k tenants
PR review, security review (if needed), and documentation for on-call
comments:
2026-03-10 — Aisha Patel: Kickoff. Collected requirements from PM and on-call (priority: early detection for enterprise customers). Agreed to prioritize top-100 tenants at minute resolution to validate sensitivity.
2026-03-11 — Diego Rivera: POC for enrichment join done (local Flink job). Observed join latency of ~120ms for cold state; we need to optimize state backend config or move tenant profile to Redis for hot tenants.
2026-03-11 — PM (Jordan Lee): Provided collection of recent incidents and annotated examples for false positives. Suggested including a lightweight model-family normalization factor to avoid false alerts during model swaps.
2026-03-12 — SRE (Maya Green): Reviewed resource implications. Recommended starting with 2 Flink task managers (8 vCPU, 32GB) for staging and adding autoscaling hooks. Raised a concern about Cassandra read amplification at high QPS; suggests adding a tenant-profile cache layer.
2026-03-12 — Diego Rivera: Implemented percentile baselining and integrated BOCPD library. Initial results on the labeled test set: true positive recall 88%, precision 82% at threshold 0.6. Need to tune threshold per-tenant-tier.
2026-03-12 — Aisha Patel: Decided to surface probabilistic severity rather than binary alerts to allow ops to tune sensitivity per project. Follow-up: create console UI for per-project sensitivity (future ticket).
